plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems and broad blue-green leaves. Late-flowering cultivars are at their peak in early May in cool temperate gardens and are grown in countless forms, including fringed, double, and parrot types.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, northeastern North America, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: During the Dutch Golden Age in the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so valuable that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house, a episode known as Tulip Mania.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub that produces dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in cold-winter climates and is often at or near peak bloom in early to mid May across much of the northern United States, Canada, and Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; widely cultivated across Europe, North America, and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilacs need a cold winter dormancy to set flower buds, and they can live for over a century, often persisting at abandoned homesteads long after the buildings are gone.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A woodland bulb that carpets the forest floor in sweeping drifts of nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented flowers, all hanging to one side of an arching stem. Peak bloom in British woodlands usually falls in late April through mid May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to late spring (late April to May)
plants.location: Atlantic Europe, especially the United Kingdom, Ireland, and northwestern France and Spain
plants.funFact: The United Kingdom holds about half of the world's bluebell population, and it is illegal to dig up wild bluebells for sale under British wildlife law.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Fern-leaved tropical to subtropical tree that is covered in trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, such as parts of Mexico, Florida, and southern Asia, early to mid May is a prime flowering time as the tree blooms at the end of the dry season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, southern California, Florida, and subtropical cities worldwide
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, the jacaranda blooms in spring are so iconic that streets and parks turn purple, and the trees were introduced there by a Japanese gardener in the early 20th century.
